prompt: An 11-person startup sells route-optimization software to independent pharmacies that run same-day prescription delivery. Eighteen pharmacies completed a ten-week paid pilot at $500 per month; twelve renewed and six did not. Pharmacy technicians use the product, owners approve purchases, patients receive deliveries, and outside courier services perform most routes. On-time delivery improved from 86% to 95% at renewed sites. Pharmacies above 2,500 monthly deliveries create 60% of compute and support cost but pay the same price as smaller sites. A regional wholesaler offers access to 600 pharmacies for a 25% revenue share, two-year exclusivity, and a custom integration. Separately, the CTO proposes building courier dispatch in-house for $600,000 over six months; the current partner API costs $0.40 per delivery and offers an SLA. Give the founders a 90-day pricing, sales/channel, and make-or-partner decision plan.
criteria: Names designing-business-models as primary, starts with an explicit primary owner and ordered handoffs, and routes billing or integration artifacts to shipping or engineering while routing post-gate channel execution to growth.

Builds separate economic records for small, high-volume, renewed, and non-renewed pharmacies, distinguishing user, buyer, payer, beneficiary, value event, willingness-to-pay evidence, sales/support effort, cost to serve, retention, and confounders.

Defines a bounded 90-day price, package, and sales-motion test with actual prices or labeled assumptions, named cohorts, an owner, review dates, numeric thresholds, and predeclared interpretations of acceptance, rejection, discounting, and churn.

Compares the wholesaler and courier boundary choices using internal-versus-partner coordination and dependency costs, exclusivity, switching, capability, delay, capital, interface, quality, and supplier-versus-architecture failure evidence before integrating or accepting the channel.

Precommits explicit pricing and boundary branches, includes a retention and accountable-effects gate, preserves a reversible option, and names the next owner for each material result rather than recommending scale or integration from access, renewal, or core-technology slogans alone.
